kapitecto.seoDescription: Kapitecto review: AI signals, a US$200 start and a demo account - checked against what the platform actually publishes.
kapitecto.deck: The promise is familiar - AI analysis, automatic execution, a US$200 entry. Kapitecto published pages decide how much of it holds.
kapitecto.depositMethods: Bank cards, bank transfer, PayPal, Skrill
intro: Kapitecto enters a crowded sector with strong advertising and a standard package. We read every public page - including the ones the marketing does not quote - and scored what we found.
Under the marketing is a working template: signup, US$200 funding, configuration, then automatic or manual trading across 11 assets with the demo running beside the live account.

We read every public page - the pricing notes, the restriction lists, the support claims and the disclosures - and scored the platform on ease of use, features, transparency, security and support. The verdict below is our own.
whatItClaims: Payouts reportedly within a day.
11 crypto assets through broker partners.
A free demo account with practice funds.
Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
whatWeChecked: The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Complete the short signup form and click the confirmation link in your inbox.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Deposit the US$200 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your risk settings, choose automatic or manual mode, and keep the demo running while you learn.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
redFlags: Support figures that contradict each other.
Template placeholders left unrendered.
Return claims without verification.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$200 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
4.6 is our number, and it means the product works with conditions attached. The demo costs nothing; use it while the claims remain unproven.
